seo.title: Best Brunch Spots in Amman (2026) | tabiji.ai
seo.metaDescription: Discover Amman's top 12 brunch spots for 2026, from traditional Jordanian to trendy international cafes. Find the perfect breakfast or late morning meal in Amman, Jordan.

hero.subtitle: Amman's brunch scene offers a vibrant mix of traditional Levantine flavors, modern international delights, and stunning city views, perfect for a leisurely morning.

picks.name: Blue Fig
picks.whyItMadeTheList: A long-standing favorite, Blue Fig is renowned for its diverse menu, vibrant atmosphere, and excellent coffee. It seamlessly blends modern decor with a cozy feel, making it perfect for a leisurely brunch with friends or family. They offer everything from classic eggs benedict to innovative salads and hearty mains.
picks.whatToOrder: Eggs Benedict with smoked salmon or their signature Berry Pancakes.
picks.insiderTip: Go early on weekends to snag a good table, especially if you want to sit on the outdoor patio. Parking can be a challenge, so consider a ride-sharing service.
picks.redditQuote: "Honestly, you can't go wrong with Blue Fig. It's my go-to for brunch in Amman. Their avocado toast is seriously next level and the vibe is always great."

picks.name: Shams El Balad
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Nestled in a beautifully restored heritage house, Shams El Balad offers an authentic taste of Jordanian hospitality and cuisine. Their commitment to using locally sourced, often organic ingredients shines through in every dish. The serene garden seating provides a picturesque backdrop for a traditional Levantine brunch.
picks.whatToOrder: Foul Medames with fresh bread, 'Manakish' with za'atar and cheese, or the delectable 'Fatteh'.
picks.insiderTip: Book a table on the terrace for stunning views of the city, especially during cooler months. Explore the small artisan shop inside for unique local crafts.
picks.redditQuote: "Shams El Balad is a must-visit for breakfast or brunch. The atmosphere is incredible, and their shakshuka is probably the best I've had in Amman. So fresh."

picks.name: Wild Jordan Center
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Part of the Royal Society for the Conservation of Nature, this cafe boasts one of the most breathtaking panoramic views of Amman from its outdoor terrace. The menu focuses on healthy, sustainable dishes often incorporating ingredients from RSCN's local initiatives. It's a peaceful escape with wholesome food.
picks.whatToOrder: The 'Jordanian Breakfast Platter' or their fresh fruit salads and smoothies.
picks.insiderTip: Combine your brunch with a stroll down Rainbow Street afterwards. Parking nearby can be tricky, so consider walking or taking a taxi.
picks.redditQuote: "If you want brunch with a view in Amman, Wild Jordan Center is it. The food is light and fresh, and the balcony view is insane. Definitely worth it."

picks.name: Fakhreldin Restaurant
picks.whyItMadeTheList: For a more opulent brunch experience, Fakhreldin offers sophisticated Lebanese cuisine in a luxurious villa setting. While known for dinner, their weekend brunch menu features an array of exquisite mezze, grilled dishes, and traditional pastries, all served with impeccable service. It's ideal for special occasions.
picks.whatToOrder: A selection of cold and hot mezze like 'Hummus with Lahmeh', 'Fatteh', and 'Kibbeh Nayyeh'.
picks.insiderTip: Dress smart-casual as it's one of Amman's more upscale establishments. Reservations are highly recommended, especially for weekend brunch.
picks.redditQuote: "My parents always take us to Fakhreldin when they visit. The Lebanese food is always top-notch, and their brunch spread is fantastic if you're looking for something a bit fancier."

picks.name: Books@Cafe
picks.whyItMadeTheList: More than just a cafe, Books@Cafe is a cultural hub offering a vast selection of books, art, and delicious food. Its bohemian vibe, eclectic decor, and rooftop terrace with city views make it a beloved spot for both locals and expats. The brunch menu is varied, catering to different tastes.
picks.whatToOrder: Their 'Halloumi & Za'atar Sandwich' or any of their generously portioned breakfast platters.
picks.insiderTip: Find a cozy corner and browse their extensive book collection while you wait for your food. The terrace is great on a sunny day.
picks.redditQuote: "Books@Cafe is my favorite chill brunch spot. Great coffee, good food, and you can just hang out for hours. Plus, the view from the roof is awesome."

picks.name: Jameeda Kitchen
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Jameeda Kitchen brings authentic Palestinian home cooking to Amman, offering a warm, inviting atmosphere reminiscent of a family kitchen. Their brunch menu is a delightful exploration of traditional Palestinian breakfast staples, prepared with love and fresh ingredients. It's a true taste of heritage.
picks.whatToOrder: The 'Musakhan Rolls' and their traditional 'Fattet Hummus', served with warm flatbread.
picks.insiderTip: Come with an appetite; portions are generous. It's a great spot to experience genuine Palestinian flavors in a cozy setting.
picks.redditQuote: "If you're craving real Palestinian comfort food for brunch, Jameeda Kitchen is the place. Their musakhan is to die for, just like teta used to make!"

picks.name: Dali Restaurant & Art Gallery
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Named after the surrealist artist, Dali is a charming spot in the bohemian neighborhood of Al Lweibdeh. It combines a lovely art gallery with a cafe offering a diverse brunch menu featuring Mediterranean and European influences. The artistic ambiance and outdoor seating make it a serene choice.
picks.whatToOrder: Their 'Shakshuka' or 'French Toast with berries and cream'.
picks.insiderTip: After brunch, take some time to explore the art on display. Parking in Lweibdeh can be challenging, so consider parking further away and enjoying a walk through the charming streets.
picks.redditQuote: "Dali in Lweibdeh is such a gem. Great for a relaxed brunch, and I always find something interesting in the gallery. Their coffee is strong too!"

picks.name: Majnoon Qahwa
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Majnoon Qahwa, meaning 'Crazy Coffee', lives up to its name with expertly crafted coffee and a fantastic selection of light brunch items. It's a modern, bustling cafe with a chic industrial aesthetic, popular with students and professionals. Perfect for a quick, quality coffee and a tasty bite.
picks.whatToOrder: Any of their specialty coffees paired with an 'Avocado Toast' or a freshly baked croissant.
picks.insiderTip: They have multiple branches; the one in Abdoun is particularly spacious. It's a great spot if you're looking to get some work done while you eat.
picks.redditQuote: "Always grab my morning coffee at Majnoon Qahwa. Their light breakfast stuff is surprisingly good for a coffee shop. That halloumi wrap is a winner."

picks.name: Rumi Cafe
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Rumi Cafe is a beloved Lweibdeh institution, known for its relaxed, artistic vibe and outdoor terrace overlooking a quiet street. It's a favorite among artists, writers, and anyone looking for a laid-back spot to enjoy good coffee and simple, delicious brunch fare. Very vegetarian-friendly.
picks.whatToOrder: Their famous 'Za'atar Manakish' or a simple 'Eggs and Cheese' platter.
picks.insiderTip: Grab a seat outside to soak in the Lweibdeh atmosphere. It's a popular spot for people-watching and enjoying the artistic energy of the neighborhood.
picks.redditQuote: "Rumi is my absolute favorite chill spot in Lweibdeh. Their za'atar mana'eesh is perfect with a black coffee, and I love just sitting there watching the world go by."

picks.name: Sufra Restaurant
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Sufra offers an elegant and authentic Jordanian dining experience in a beautifully restored villa. While known for its lunch and dinner, their traditional brunch spread is a feast for the senses, featuring an array of Jordanian staples in a refined setting. The garden seating is particularly charming.
picks.whatToOrder: The 'Sufra Breakfast Platter' which includes a variety of local delights like labneh, za'atar, and olives.
picks.insiderTip: Make reservations, especially for weekend brunch, to secure a table in their picturesque garden. It's a bit pricier but worth it for the ambiance and quality.
picks.redditQuote: "If you want to impress someone with traditional Jordanian food and a gorgeous setting, Sufra's brunch is it. A bit expensive but truly beautiful experience."

picks.name: Al Quds Restaurant
picks.whyItMadeTheList: For a truly authentic, budget-friendly Amman brunch experience, Al Quds is a downtown institution. Famous for its legendary falafel and hummus, this no-frills spot offers a bustling, energetic atmosphere. It's where locals go for a quick, delicious, and incredibly affordable breakfast or early lunch.
picks.whatToOrder: A classic 'Falafel Sandwich' with fresh mint and pickles, or a hearty plate of 'Hummus with Foul'.
picks.insiderTip: Go with cash as credit cards aren't typically accepted. Expect a crowd, especially around peak brunch hours, but the service is quick.
picks.redditQuote: "Forget fancy brunch, just go to Al Quds downtown. Best falafel in Amman, hands down. It's cheap, fast, and exactly what you need after a late night."

picks.name: The Coffee Bean & Tea Leaf
picks.whyItMadeTheList: A familiar name for many, The Coffee Bean & Tea Leaf offers reliable Western-style brunch options across its numerous Amman locations. It's a comfortable and consistent choice for those seeking classic breakfast sandwiches, pastries, or a good cup of coffee in a relaxed, casual setting. Great for a quick, fuss-free meal.
picks.whatToOrder: Their 'Egg & Cheese Bagel' or a fresh 'Muffin' with a brewed coffee or flavored latte.
picks.insiderTip: Ideal for a quick bite or if you're looking for familiar options and free Wi-Fi. Check which branch is closest to your location as they are widely spread.
picks.redditQuote: "Sometimes you just want something familiar, right? Coffee Bean & Tea Leaf is my go-to for a decent breakfast sandwich and a reliable cappuccino when I'm not feeling adventurous."

faq.question: What is a typical brunch like in Amman?
faq.answer: Brunch in Amman is a delightful blend of traditional Levantine flavors and modern international cuisine. You can expect to find classic dishes like foul medames (fava bean stew), hummus, labneh, shakshuka, and manakish (flatbreads with toppings), alongside Western favorites such as eggs benedict, pancakes, and avocado toast. Many places also offer fresh juices, strong Arabic coffee, and various teas, all enjoyed in a relaxed, often social atmosphere.

faq.question: Are there vegetarian and vegan options available at Amman brunch spots?
faq.answer: Absolutely! Amman is quite vegetarian-friendly, especially at traditional brunch spots where many staple dishes like foul, hummus, falafel, and various salads are naturally vegetarian or vegan. Many modern cafes also explicitly offer vegetarian and vegan options, including plant-based milks for coffee and dedicated menu items. Always ask your server for clarification or modifications if needed.

faq.question: What's the best time to go for brunch in Amman?
faq.answer: Brunch in Amman typically kicks off around 10:00 AM and can last until 2:00 PM or even later on weekends. For popular spots, arriving closer to 10:00 AM or 10:30 AM on Fridays and Saturdays (the weekend in Jordan) is recommended to avoid peak crowds and secure a good table. Weekday brunches are generally more relaxed and less busy.

faq.question: Do I need reservations for brunch in Amman?
faq.answer: For highly popular or upscale brunch spots, especially on Friday and Saturday, making a reservation is strongly advised to guarantee a table. This is particularly true for places with outdoor seating or desirable views. For more casual cafes or traditional eateries, reservations are often not required, but expect a short wait during peak hours.

faq.question: Is alcohol served at brunch spots in Amman?
faq.answer: While many cafes and traditional restaurants in Amman do not serve alcohol, you can find it at several international hotels and more upscale restaurants. For brunch, spots like Blue Fig or Fakhreldin may offer alcoholic beverages, but it's always best to check their menu or call ahead if this is a key factor for your brunch plans.

faq.question: What areas of Amman are best for brunch?
faq.answer: Several neighborhoods in Amman are excellent for brunch. Jabal Amman (especially around Rainbow Street) and Al Lweibdeh are popular for their charming, bohemian cafes and traditional eateries. Abdoun is known for its more modern, upscale, and international brunch options. Downtown offers authentic, budget-friendly traditional breakfast and brunch experiences.

methodology: Our selection of Amman's best brunch spots is based on extensive local research, diner reviews across multiple platforms, and direct visits. We prioritized venues offering high-quality food, unique ambiance, excellent service, and value, ensuring a diverse representation of culinary styles and price points for every preference.
